article.title: How to Install Solar Path Lights That Actually Work
article.summary: Install solar path lights that shine all night: pick sunny spots, space them evenly, stake them without breaking them and keep the panels clean.
article.body:
Solar path lights need no wiring, no trench and no outlet. Whether they glow all night or fade by 9 p.m. depends mostly on where you put them. This guide covers stake-mounted solar lights along walks, driveways and beds.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: keep lights out of the mower's path and away from spots where people step off the walk. Only push stakes a few inches deep; if you plan to dig deeper anywhere, call 811 first to have buried utility lines marked.

Steps

  1. Find spots with full sun

    Watch the path on a sunny day. Each light's panel needs several hours of direct sun, ideally 6 to 8. Avoid spots shaded by shrubs, eaves or fences, and keep them away from porch lights or streetlights, which can stop the sensor from turning them on.

    Done right: every planned spot gets direct sun for most of the day.

  2. Plan the spacing

    Space lights about 6 to 8 ft apart, and stagger them on both sides of the path instead of lining one side like a runway. Mark the spots with the stakes or small flags.

    Done right: the lights will make even pools of light without dark gaps.

  3. Switch them on and charge them

    Assemble each light, pull any battery tab and move the switch to ON. Let them charge in full sun for a day or two before judging how long they last.

    Done right: each light turns on when you cover its panel with your hand.

  4. Stake them without breaking them

    Plastic stakes snap when hammered into hard soil. Make a pilot hole first with a trowel or screwdriver, then push the stake in by hand, tapping the base gently with a rubber mallet if needed. Keep each light straight and the panel facing up.

    Done right: the lights stand straight and don't wobble.

  5. Maintain them

    Wipe the panels with a damp cloth every month or two, because dust and pollen cut charging. Replace the rechargeable batteries with the same type and size every year or two when run time drops.

    Done right: the lights stay on well into the night.

Consider low-voltage lighting if: your path is mostly shaded or you want brighter, more reliable light. See our low-voltage path light guide, or hire a landscape lighting installer for a large yard.

FAQ

How many hours of sun do solar lights need?

Several hours of direct sun, ideally 6 to 8, to run through most of the night.

Why do my solar lights stop working?

Common causes are shade, dirty panels, worn-out rechargeable batteries, or a nearby light that confuses the sensor.

How far apart should solar path lights be?

About 6 to 8 ft apart, staggered along both sides of the path.

Can I replace solar light batteries?

Usually, yes. Use rechargeable batteries of the same type and size. Regular alkaline batteries won't recharge.
